html:
Remark. Spectral characterisation, the Chern--Simons correction, and the open bare residual

Spectral characterisation. Three structural results establish the existence and uniqueness of the electromagnetic fine structure constant:

  1. Two-strand spectral completeness (completeness theorem). The algebra \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A \otimes A) has R-rank 2. Exactly two central idempotents e_+, e_- sum to \mathrm{id}. Plancherel completeness w_+ + w_- = 1 exhausts the Frobenius mass. No third channel exists.
  2. Uniqueness of the gauge coupling (corollary, ibid.). The singlet idempotent e_- is the unique scalar exchange channel. Any R-linear braid-invariant scalar coupling A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1} is a multiple of \mathrm{tr}_\tau(e_-) \cdot e_-. The constant \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} exists and is unique up to global normalisation. The antisymmetric eigenvalue captures the entirety of the electromagnetic coupling.
  3. Force-carrier uniqueness (Bring uniqueness). The set \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\} exhausts genus-4 torus knots. This is a Diophantine fact: the equation (m-1)(n-1)=8 with \gcd(m,n)=1 and m \leq n has only the solutions (2,9) and (3,5). The Bring-supported quantum observable universe has a forced force-carrier sector with categorical complexity [9]_q \cdot [10]_q \in R.

These results turn \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} into a topological invariant of the Bring fibration. At the fundamental level, no contour integrals, no factors of 2 \pi i, and no renormalisation-group running are required.

Descent decomposition: Chern-Simons correction.

The bare formula \alpha^{-1} = q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q gives the base holonomy of the electromagnetic endomorphism. This is the bulk coupling from the R-matrix eigenvalue multiplied by the q-deformed crossing complexities. It is the analogue of the volume term \lambda_V \cdot A in the mass formula.

The full coupling receives an exceptional divisor correction from the Chern-Simons invariants of the force-carrier torus knots T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} (EM coupling Chern-Simons):

  \frac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}}
  =
  q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q
  \cdot \bigl(1 + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}
               + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^2 \cdot \kappa\bigr)

where

  \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}
  =
  \frac{\bigl(\mathrm{CS}(T_{2,9}) + \mathrm{CS}(T_{3,5})\bigr)
        \cdot \tfrac{[2]_q}{2} \cdot \hbar_q^2}
       {q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q}

and \kappa = \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\mathrm{cl}} / \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{q} \approx 1.722 is the Gram determinant ratio of the classical and q-deformed Chern–Simons pairing. It captures self-dual damping at the second jet level. Both \delta_{\mathrm{CS}} and \kappa derive from the Chern–Simons invariants and the Bring-surface Gram matrix. No free parameters are introduced (EM coupling Chern-Simons).

The universal formula gives the Chern-Simons invariants of torus knots T_{m,n}:

  \mathrm{CS}(T_{m,n})
  =
  \frac{\pi^2 (m^2 - 1)(n^2 - 1)}{12\,m\,n}.

This yields \mathrm{CS}(T_{2,9}) = \pi^2 \cdot \tfrac{10}{9} and \mathrm{CS}(T_{3,5}) = \pi^2 \cdot \tfrac{16}{15}. The quantum Planck constant is \hbar_q = (q - 1)/q.

Numerical evaluation.

See Table 1.

The Chern-Simons correction reduces the discrepancy from 0.155\% (bare formula) to 399\;\mathrm{ppb}. However, the \kappa \approx 1.722 value was admitted as sorry in the Lean formalisation and never closed. Exact matching with CODATA requires \kappa \approx 1.8878. See rem:em-coupling-chern-simons for the demoted statement and open problems for the path forward.

Open problem: closing the 0.155\% bare residual. The bare formula 1/\alpha_{\text{bare}} = q\cdot[9]_q\cdot[10]_q has a complete categorical derivation. It accounts for \alpha_{\text{EM}} to -0.155\% at q_0. The remaining \sim 1.55 \times 10^{-3} relative gap lacks a closed structural derivation:

  1. The Chern-Simons form (1+\delta_{CS}+\kappa\delta_{CS}^2) is conjectural. The \kappa identification is unproved. Both the 2{\times}2 J^2-jet derivation and the Wedderburn-block Plancherel sum yield \kappa \approx 1.722. This falls short of the \kappa \approx 1.888 needed for CODATA. Block-diagonal Gram deformations cannot close this gap. See rem:alpha-em-derivation-open-problems for the multiplicative-family ruling.
  2. The PSLQ-empirical form 45[3]_q(1+\hbar_q^4[5]_q+8q(\hbar_q^4[5]_q)^2) matches CODATA to 7 ppb at q_0. It disagrees with the bare formula at every other q. Only one of its four factors is structurally derived. It is superseded by the additive Bring zero-mode form.
  3. The additive Bring zero-mode form (prop:em-coupling-bring-zero-mode): 1/\alpha_{EM} = q[9]_q[10]_q + 2g/(4\pi(g-1)) + \mathcal{O}(\alpha) at g=4. The correction 2g/(4\pi(g-1)) = 2/(3\pi) admits two geometric identifications: the Hodge / Gauss-Bonnet ratio on Bring's surface, and the sphere-volume ratio \mathrm{Vol}(S^2)/(3\,\mathrm{Vol}(S^3)). The single-term relative residual is -4.2 \times 10^{-6}. With the next-order \alpha/(4\pi) term, it is +5.7 \times 10^{-8}. This is the numerical front-runner. It imports the archimedean transcendental \pi via sphere volumes and Hodge data. This puts the correction structurally outside the pre-archimedean substrate ring R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}]. Its pre-archimedean status is open. See prop:archimedean-functor-uniqueness for the repair route, which factors the state sum through a Bloch-group class using substrate pentagon-coherence.

The bare q[9]_q[10]_q derivation is solid and pre-archimedean. Closing the remaining 1.55 \times 10^{-3} gap requires a pre-archimedean origin for the \pi-bearing additive correction or an off-diagonal Gram deformation that escapes the multiplicative-family ruling. Neither is established.
